personas.name: The Screening Associate
personas.context: The analyst who assembles the foundational borrower profile end to end, on a 48-72 hour clock, before anyone senior sees it. Opens with the entity name and no context: checks Capital IQ and Bloomberg to establish public or private, then the internal CRM, Salesforce and the credit document repository for any prior firm contact. Builds the org chart by hand from PDF credit agreements and pitch books, re-keys financials into an Excel template, and only reaches the actual risk analysis late on the second night. Interviewed directly; every trait below is his own account of his own work.
goals: Reach the leverage math and the investment thesis while there is still time to think about them, instead of at midnight on day two
Establish on day one whether the firm has touched this client, its sponsors or its subsidiaries before
Get the covenant definitions, debt schedule and EBITDA definition out of the credit agreement without reading 300 pages
Hand the reviewer a profile that survives first contact, so no rework loop starts
Stop the clock running while he waits on a sponsor reply he cannot chase directly
frustrations: Roughly 70% of the window goes to finding and formatting data and only 30% to analysis
Mapping the ultimate parent, co-issuers and guarantors of a PE-backed structure alone consumes 4 to 5 hours of the first day
Financials arrive as PDFs to be copied by hand into a template whose formulas break
An incomplete submission from the sponsor stalls him for 24 hours while his own deadline keeps moving
Time spent on font consistency is time spent anticipating a reviewer's objection rather than answering it
personas.quote: I feel like a glorified data entry clerk for the first two days.

personas.name: The Credit Risk Reviewer
personas.context: The director who signs off — or does not — on the finished profile, in a 20 to 30 minute initial review that gates the Credit Committee date. Reads in a fixed order: total leverage ratio and how adjusted EBITDA was built, then liquidity runway across cash and revolver capacity, then the corporate structure and guarantee package. Skips the company history outright. Interviewed directly.
goals: Confirm in the first minutes who is actually on the hook for the debt and whether cash is leaking to unrated offshore subsidiaries
Check an add-back or a pro-forma adjustment against its source without reopening the underlying agreement
Complete an initial review in five minutes rather than thirty, with more confidence rather than less
Return a defect without triggering a rework loop that moves the committee date
frustrations: Vendor pulls accepted without adjusting for pro-forma numbers from a recent acquisition
Management EBITDA add-backs taken at face value — a 'one-time' fee that recurred three years running
A single caught error costs her confidence in the whole file, not just the line it appeared on
Static PDFs and Word documents that cannot be interrogated, so verification means reopening a 300-page agreement herself
Fixing small defects personally to avoid a round of email that would cost more than the fix
personas.quote: If I catch an error like that, I lose trust in the whole profile.

personas.name: The Managing Director
personas.context: Runs large-scale corporate lending and opportunistic credit, and carries the position after the deal is booked. Frames the team's constraint as speed and informational symmetry rather than capital allocation. Consumes the Associate's screening work as a decision input and the portfolio's risk posture as a standing feed. Interviewed directly. Deployment isolation is his stated precondition for adoption at all.
goals: Issue term sheets faster than competing lenders, because speed is what wins the deal in this market
See what another desk already learned about a target at the moment of screening, not after
Catch distress while a workout or refinancing can still be structured — see smoke before there is a fire
Receive a risk signal that already contains the decision: the issue, the exposure, and the trigger point
Keep proprietary deal data inside the firm's own cloud perimeter
frustrations: Initial vetting takes three days because the inputs are scattered across filings, private databases, relationship logs and macro feeds
Another desk's prior coverage sits in a legacy PDF or a personal Outlook inbox, invisible exactly when it would create leverage
Covenant compliance is keyed quarterly into spreadsheets, so a breach surfaces about three months after the fact
Monitoring products present fifty simultaneous flags and leave the interpretation to him
personas.quote: We lose massive leverage by not knowing what the firm already knows.

actions: Receives the entity name and opens a tracking spreadsheet
Checks Capital IQ and Bloomberg to establish whether the company is public or private
Scopes how much of the structure will have to be built by hand
journey.emotion: Apprehension — the size of the build is clear before any of it is possible
friction: No indication yet whether the firm has prior history with this name
Coverage quality for a mid-market private borrower is unknown until he is already inside the vendor tools

actions: Searches the internal CRM and Salesforce for the client, its sponsors and its subsidiaries
Searches the credit document repository for prior agreements
Asks colleagues informally where older coverage might sit
journey.emotion: Low-grade doubt — he cannot tell the difference between no history and history he failed to find
friction: Prior work stored in a personal Outlook inbox or a local drive is unreachable by any search he can run
Another desk's coverage of a subsidiary two years ago is invisible unless someone remembers it

actions: Parses hundreds of pages of PDF credit agreements and pitch books
Traces the ultimate parent, co-issuers and guarantors and draws the org chart in PowerPoint
Copies financials out of PDFs into the Excel template
journey.emotion: Grinding — the work is legible as effort and illegible as judgment
friction: Four to five hours of the first day go to the org chart alone
The template's formulas break under manual entry
Nothing he transcribes carries a pointer back to the sentence it came from
journey.current_metric: Four to five hours of day one go to the org chart alone (associate interviews)

journey.stage: Modelling and thesis under a live clock (Associate)
actions: Calculates leverage metrics and evaluates industry headwinds
Writes the investment thesis
Emails the deal team for a missing cash flow statement or footnotes and waits
journey.emotion: Pressure — the analysis he was hired for begins on the second night
friction: A sponsor reply can take 24 hours while his own deadline does not move
He cannot chase the sponsor directly; the request routes through the deal team
Formatting consumes time that anticipates an objection rather than answering it

journey.stage: Risk review and verification (Credit Risk Reviewer)
actions: Reads total leverage ratio and interrogates the adjusted EBITDA add-backs
Checks liquidity runway across cash and revolver capacity
Examines the corporate structure and guarantee package for unrated offshore subsidiaries
Skims past the company overview entirely
journey.emotion: Guarded — reading for the one thing that will invalidate the rest
friction: Verifying any single number means reopening the 300-page agreement herself
An unadjusted pro-forma pull or an unquestioned add-back costs her trust in the whole file
Twenty to thirty minutes is spent establishing confidence rather than forming a view
journey.current_metric: Twenty to thirty minutes per risk review, verification reopening the 300-page agreement (reviewer interview)

journey.stage: Defect return and rework loop (Reviewer and Associate)
actions: Fixes minor formatting issues herself to avoid a round of email
Returns the file when the leverage math is wrong
Associate reworks against a deadline that has already partly elapsed
journey.emotion: Strain on both sides — she is spending her time on his work, he is redoing work he thought was finished
friction: Sign-off slips, the Credit Committee is postponed, and a live closing date comes into question
The correction travels as email, so the cost of returning a defect is weighed against just absorbing it

actions: Receives borrower-submitted covenant figures quarterly and has them keyed into spreadsheets
Reviews compliance calculations at the quarterly cycle
Scans monitoring dashboards for anything that warrants attention
journey.emotion: Reactive — informed of conditions that have already settled
friction: A breach or a dip in coverage ratios surfaces roughly three months after it happened, past the point where a workout can be structured
Fifty simultaneous flags carry no ranking, no exposure figure and no distance to the covenant threshold
journey.current_metric: A breach or coverage dip surfaces roughly three months after it happened (MD interview)

hmw_statements.statement: How might we make a firm's own prior contact with a target visible at the moment someone starts evaluating it, including the contact nobody remembers?
How might we shorten the distance between a term written into a credit agreement and a number an analyst can act on?
How might we let a reviewer satisfy themselves that a figure is right without leaving the profile they are reading?
How might we keep the deal clock from being held hostage to a reply that has not arrived?
How might we make a portfolio signal arrive early enough, and specific enough, to change what a Managing Director does that day?
